cues.en: Hey there, it's Asma Khalid, one of the hosts of The Global Story podcast from the BBC.
cues.zh: 大家好，我是阿斯玛·哈立德，是 BBC《全球故事》播客的主持人之一。

cues.en: And as a bonus for your feed, we're bringing you one of our favorite episodes of the week.
cues.zh: 作为你订阅内容的加餐，我们带来本周最喜欢的一期节目。

cues.en: Now every weekday on The Global Story, we try to tell one big story in depth about where the world and America intersect.
cues.zh: 《全球故事》每个工作日都会深入讲述一个大故事，探讨世界与美国交汇之处。

cues.en: In this episode, we look at a scientific breakthrough that comes with a lot of baggage here in the US:
cues.zh: 本期我们关注一项科学突破，但它在美国背负着沉重的政治包袱：

cues.en: a vaccine for skin cancer that has shown promising results in a recent clinical trial.
cues.zh: 一种治疗皮肤癌的疫苗，最近的临床试验显示出令人鼓舞的结果。

cues.en: What's notable is that this is an mRNA vaccine, and you all might recognize that term, mRNA,
cues.zh: 值得注意的是，这是一种信使 RNA 疫苗；大家可能听过 mRNA 这个词，

cues.en: because it's the same technology that was used in some COVID vaccines.
cues.zh: 因为一些新冠疫苗就采用了同样的技术。

cues.en: And that is what is making this new scientific breakthrough so politically tricky.
cues.zh: 正因如此，这项新的科学突破在政治上变得棘手。

cues.en: The COVID vaccines led to the rise of vaccine skepticism within the highest ranks of the US government,
cues.zh: 新冠疫苗催生了美国政府最高层中的疫苗怀疑论，

cues.en: complicating the future of this potentially life-saving new research in America and around the world.
cues.zh: 使这项可能挽救生命的新研究在美国和世界各地的前景更加复杂。

cues.en: So, I hope you'll take a listen to this episode. And if you enjoy it, you can always find more from us by searching for "The Global Story" wherever you get your podcasts.
cues.zh: 希望大家收听这一期节目。如果你喜欢，随时可以在收听播客的平台搜索《全球故事》，找到我们的更多内容。

cues.en: Now, on to today's show.
cues.zh: 现在进入今天的节目。

cues.en: It was 1997 at the University of Pennsylvania in Philly.
cues.zh: 那是1997年，在费城的宾夕法尼亚大学。

cues.en: A Hungarian American scientist by the name of Dr Katalin Karikó was wandering the halls looking for a copy machine.
cues.zh: 一位名叫卡塔琳·考里科的匈牙利裔美国科学家，在走廊里寻找复印机。

cues.en: And when she found one, she came across another researcher. They struck up a conversation.
cues.zh: 找到复印机后，她遇到了另一位研究人员，两人聊了起来。

cues.en: And so I was bragging that I've worked with RNA.
cues.zh: 所以我当时夸耀说，我一直在研究 RNA。

cues.en: And then he was telling me that he want to develop a vaccine. And that's how, you know, we started.
cues.zh: 然后他告诉我，他想开发一种疫苗。就这样，你知道，我们开始合作了。

cues.en: Dr Karikó and her research partner would go on to spend years working together on what was sometimes a scientific dead end: an mRNA vaccine.
cues.zh: 卡塔琳·考里科博士和她的研究伙伴后来花了多年时间，共同研究一种有时近乎科学死胡同的方案：信使 RNA 疫苗。

cues.en: For years, their efforts amounted to little.
cues.zh: 多年来，他们的努力收效甚微。

cues.en: But in 2023, after the development of the COVID vaccines that used mRNA technology, they were awarded the Nobel Prize for Medicine.
cues.zh: 但在采用信使 RNA 技术的新冠疫苗研发成功后，他们于2023年获得了诺贝尔生理学或医学奖。

cues.en: Together, they have saved millions of lives.
cues.zh: 他们共同挽救了数百万人的生命。

cues.en: They prevented severe COVID-19, reduced the overall disease burden, and enabled societies to open up again.
cues.zh: 他们预防了重症新冠，减轻了总体疾病负担，也让社会得以重新开放。

cues.en: Last week, there was another watershed moment from that same mRNA technology: a potential cancer vaccine.
cues.zh: 上周，同一种信使 RNA 技术又迎来一个里程碑时刻：一种潜在的癌症疫苗。

cues.en: And yet the news comes in a tough climate for vaccines.
cues.zh: 然而，这一消息传出之际，正值疫苗面临艰难环境。

cues.en: Last year, the US Health and Human Services Secretary, RFK Jr., cut half a billion dollars of funding into mRNA research.
cues.zh: 去年，美国卫生与公众服务部长小罗伯特·F·肯尼迪削减了用于信使 RNA 研究的5亿美元资金。

cues.en: From the BBC, I'm Asma Khalid in Washington, D.C.
cues.zh: 这里是 BBC，我是来自华盛顿特区的阿斯玛·哈立德。

cues.en: And today on The Global Story, the new skin cancer vaccine, and the promise and politics of mRNA technology.
cues.zh: 今天的《全球故事》将讨论新的皮肤癌疫苗，以及信使 RNA 技术的前景与政治。

cues.en: I'm Tom Whipple. I'm a science writer, and I present Inside Science on BBC Radio 4 and the World Service.
cues.zh: 我是汤姆·惠普尔。我是科学作家，主持 BBC Radio 4 和世界服务台的《Inside Science》。

cues.en: Well, Tom Whipple, welcome to The Global Story. It's a pleasure to have you with us. Thanks for taking the time. It's a pleasure.
cues.zh: 汤姆·惠普尔，欢迎来到《全球故事》。很高兴你参加我们的节目，感谢你抽出时间。我的荣幸。

cues.en: Today on the show, we want to dive into the health and policy debates around mRNA technology.
cues.zh: 今天我们要深入探讨围绕信使 RNA 技术的健康与政策争论。

cues.en: Particularly here in the United States where I sit in this political moment.
cues.zh: 尤其是在我所在的美国，以及当前这个政治时刻。

cues.en: But the reason that we wanted to have this conversation today is because of a major medical breakthrough that made headlines just the other day.
cues.zh: 但我们今天想展开这场对话，是因为前几天一项重大的医学突破登上了新闻头条。

cues.en: What is being described is a personalized cancer vaccine.
cues.zh: 这项突破被描述为一种个性化癌症疫苗。

cues.en: Now, to be abundantly clear to listeners, it is not like you or I, Tom, could take a jab and have immunity from developing skin cancer.
cues.zh: 这里要向听众明确说明：它并不是说你、我或汤姆打一针，就能获得免于患皮肤癌的免疫力。

cues.en: This is a different type of vaccine.
cues.zh: 这是一种不同类型的疫苗。

cues.en: Nonetheless, I'm hearing it described as a game-changer.
cues.zh: 尽管如此，我听到有人把它称为改变游戏规则的突破。

cues.en: Can you explain what was actually announced and why it is being seen as so significant?
cues.zh: 你能解释一下究竟公布了什么，以及为什么它被视为如此重要吗？

cues.en: Yeah, so as you say, this isn't—this isn't you getting a summer booster shot and then being unable to catch skin cancer for that summer. It's absolutely not that.
cues.zh: 是的，正如你所说，这不是说你打一针夏季加强针，就能在那个夏天免于感染皮肤癌。绝对不是这样。

cues.en: There is a reason which we'll get into why the word vaccine is still perfectly appropriate.
cues.zh: 我们稍后会解释，为什么使用“疫苗”这个词仍然完全恰当。

cues.en: But what this is is that you—if you've got a skin cancer, or, you know, in theory, we'd like this to work for lots of cancers,
cues.zh: 但它的原理是：如果你患有皮肤癌——理论上，我们希望它能适用于许多癌症——

cues.en: you remove it, but the real worry is it comes back.
cues.zh: 你会先切除肿瘤，但真正令人担心的是它复发。

cues.en: We all know about metastases and the idea that cancer spreads in the body even after you've removed it.
cues.zh: 我们都知道癌症会转移，也知道即使切除了肿瘤，癌细胞仍可能在体内扩散。

cues.en: What this is doing is it is training your body to attack it.
cues.zh: 这种疫苗是在训练你的身体去攻击它。

cues.en: It's training it to attack the cancer cells that are there in the tumour.
cues.zh: 它训练身体攻击肿瘤中的癌细胞。

cues.en: So that your body's own defenses take it out.
cues.zh: 让你身体自身的防御系统将其消灭。

cues.en: And so in that sense, it's very much like a vaccine. The idea of a vaccine is: you show your body a little bit of the thing that you want to attack.
cues.zh: 所以从这个意义上说，它非常像疫苗：疫苗的原理是，让身体接触一点你想要攻击的对象。

cues.en: And then your immune system's trained and away it goes and attacks it.
cues.zh: 然后你的免疫系统受到训练，随即发动攻击。

cues.en: This is a really big deal. So the caveats are we don't yet know how well this worked.
cues.zh: 这确实意义重大。但需要注意的是，我们还不知道它的效果究竟有多好。

cues.en: We know this has gone through phase three trials, which is the final stage of trials
cues.zh: 我们知道它已经完成了三期试验，这是试验的最后阶段，

cues.en: before you can introduce a drug or a treatment.
cues.zh: 在你能够推出一种药物或治疗之前。

cues.en: We know that the companies that made it.
cues.zh: 我们知道，研发它的公司是……

cues.en: Merck and Moderna are confident that this is clinically significant and useful.
cues.zh: 默沙东和莫德纳相信，这一疗法具有重要的临床意义且切实有用。

cues.en: It prevented cancer from returning in a significant number of patients. It helped them live longer.
cues.zh: 它阻止相当一部分患者的癌症复发，也帮助他们活得更久。

cues.en: This isn't a magic bullet, but the reason it's so significant is because doctors have been trying to do this for 30, 40 years.
cues.zh: 这不是灵丹妙药，但它意义重大，因为医生们已经尝试这样做了三四十年。

cues.en: They've been trying to make a cancer vaccine because it is such a simple and appealing idea, and it seems like it should work.
cues.zh: 他们一直想研制癌症疫苗，因为这是个简单而诱人的想法，看起来本该奏效。

cues.en: And until now, largely, they've failed. So the fact that this has succeeded,
cues.zh: 而在此之前，他们基本都失败了。所以这次取得成功，

cues.en: and in particular succeeded using mRNA technology, which is this big coming technology,
cues.zh: 尤其是借助这种前景巨大的 mRNA 技术取得成功，

cues.en: suggests that we could be on the cusp of having a new wing to our cancer treatments,
cues.zh: 这表明，我们或许正处在癌症治疗开创新方向的边缘，

cues.en: and also a wing that's a lot more gentle than many of the treatments that we're used to.
cues.zh: 而且这个方向会比我们熟悉的许多疗法温和得多。

cues.en: So, just to make sure I'm following here, Tom, this has gone through all the necessary trials.
cues.zh: 汤姆，我确认一下：它已经完成了所有必要的试验。

cues.en: It has not yet, this vaccine, received the approval here in the United States
cues.zh: 但这款疫苗还没有在美国获得批准，

cues.en: from the FDA, the Food and Drug Administration,
cues.zh: 批准机构是 FDA，即美国食品药品监督管理局；

cues.en: but it looks like it's on track to be possibly used by the public in the near future.
cues.zh: 但它似乎有望在不久的将来供公众使用。

cues.en: Yeah, once you've gone through phase three trials and been successful in your determination,
cues.zh: 是的，一旦完成三期试验并在评估中取得成功，

cues.en: that's when you gather together all of the data that you've got and you present it to the regulator and you say,
cues.zh: 就要把掌握的全部数据汇总起来，提交给监管机构，并告诉他们：

cues.en: Ta-da! We think we've made something that you will want.
cues.zh: 看，我们认为自己研发出了你们会需要的东西。

cues.en: And then it is up to the regulator to say, Yes, you have, or Yes, you haven't.
cues.zh: 然后就由监管机构决定：是的，你们做到了；或者，不，你们没有做到。

cues.en: But look, if you want a sense of the confidence in this, you just have to look at Moderna's share price.
cues.zh: 不过，要感受人们对它的信心，只要看看莫德纳的股价就知道了。

cues.en: Oh yes, you know, this is...
cues.zh: 哦，是的，你知道，这是一件……

cues.en: something where people are betting a lot of billions that actually they've got something that works.
cues.zh: 人们押上数十亿美元，赌的就是他们真的研发出了有效的东西。

cues.en: So it sounds like we might need to be cautious still, but it sounds like we can be cautiously optimistic at this point.
cues.zh: 所以我们似乎仍需谨慎，但在这一阶段也可以谨慎乐观。

cues.en: Can you walk us through exactly how this is different from the way that a traditional vaccine would work?
cues.zh: 你能具体讲讲，这和传统疫苗的工作方式究竟有何不同吗？

cues.en: So, all vaccines, the principle is that your immune system learns by seeing things.
cues.zh: 所有疫苗的原理都是一样的：免疫系统通过观察事物来学习。

cues.en: Now, if I get infected by measles, my immune system will learn what the outside of a measles virus looks like,
cues.zh: 如果我感染麻疹，我的免疫系统就会了解麻疹病毒外表是什么样，

cues.en: and provided that measles hasn't killed me, when I then see measles again, my immune system will know exactly what to do with it.
cues.zh: 只要麻疹没有杀死我，下次再遇到它时，我的免疫系统就会知道该怎么应对。

cues.en: It will have the antibodies and T cells ready to chomp it up, get rid of it, and I am completely immune from measles.
cues.zh: 抗体和 T 细胞会准备好将其吞噬、清除，而我也就对麻疹完全免疫了。

cues.en: Okay. The principle of a vaccine is to do that without having the 'provided I'm still alive' bit.
cues.zh: 好。疫苗的原理，就是不用经历“前提是我还活着”这一环节，也能做到这一点。

cues.en: Excellent, yes. It's to show you what a virus, a pathogen, or some sort of bacteria looks like
cues.zh: 没错。它向你展示病毒、病原体或某种细菌是什么样，

cues.en: without actually getting you the infection bit, so there are lots of ways of doing this.
cues.zh: 却不让你真正感染，因此有很多种实现方式。

cues.en: Normally, what you do is get an attenuated version of the virus.
cues.zh: 通常的做法，是使用一种减毒版病毒。

cues.en: What they've done is they've serially bred the virus to make it weaker and weaker,
cues.zh: 具体来说，他们连续培育这种病毒，让它变得越来越弱，

cues.en: and so it doesn't give you measles, but it looks similar enough to the measles virus that does give you measles
cues.zh: 这样它不会让你患麻疹，但外形又足够像真正会致病的麻疹病毒，

cues.en: that having had it, your immune system knows exactly what to do with the real thing when it turns up.
cues.zh: 让你的免疫系统在真正的病毒出现时，知道该如何应对。

cues.en: You have to develop that specifically for that particular virus.
cues.zh: 你必须针对那一种特定病毒专门开发它。

cues.en: But the thing that made mRNA different is that they were programmable vaccines.
cues.zh: 但 mRNA 的不同之处在于，它能制造可编程的疫苗。

cues.en: Okay.
cues.zh: 好。

cues.en: So there is something that's known as the central dogma of biology, and it is DNA makes RNA makes proteins.
cues.zh: 生物学中有个概念叫“中心法则”：DNA 产生 RNA，RNA 产生蛋白质。

cues.en: And what proteins do is make the body work.
cues.zh: 而蛋白质的作用，就是让身体运转起来。

cues.en: So I think almost all listeners will be familiar with DNA.
cues.zh: 我想，几乎所有听众都熟悉 DNA。

cues.en: It is, very crudely, the blueprint of you.
cues.zh: 非常粗略地说，它就是你的蓝图。

cues.en: DNA is like the instruction manual, the thing you get when you get flat-pack furniture.
cues.zh: DNA 就像说明书，就像你买平板包装家具时附带的那本说明书。

cues.en: But the instruction manual isn't enough unless you have the person to read it and then turn the flat-pack furniture into the bookshelf.
cues.zh: 但光有说明书还不够，还需要有人读懂它，再把平板家具组装成书架。

cues.en: And that's sort of what RNA, or messenger RNA, that's where it comes in.
cues.zh: 这就是 RNA，也就是信使 RNA 发挥作用的地方。

cues.en: So there was this idea: could we hijack this process?
cues.zh: 于是有人提出了一个想法：我们能不能劫持这个过程？

cues.en: One of the pioneers of this idea was a Hungarian scientist called Katalin Karikó.
cues.zh: 这一想法的先驱之一，是一位名叫卡塔琳·考里科的匈牙利科学家。

cues.en: I grew up in Hungary in a very sleepy small town.
cues.zh: 我在匈牙利一个非常宁静的小镇长大。

cues.en: We did not have running water, a television set, a refrigerator, and so on,
cues.zh: 我们没有自来水、电视、冰箱之类的东西，

cues.en: but nobody had, so I didn't know we don't have.
cues.zh: 但大家都没有，所以我不知道我们是没有这些东西。

cues.en: She'd been plugging away at this from 1985.
cues.zh: 从 1985 年起，她就一直埋头钻研这个领域。

cues.en: You know, she studied this at university in Hungary.
cues.zh: 她曾在匈牙利的大学研究这个领域。

cues.en: Quite dramatically, she couldn't do the research she wanted in Hungary.
cues.zh: 很遗憾，她无法在匈牙利开展自己想做的研究。

cues.en: She left with $1,000 sewn inside a teddy bear, along with her family, to go and do the research she wanted to do.
cues.zh: 她和家人一起离开匈牙利，把 1000 美元缝在一只泰迪熊里，去做自己想做的研究。

cues.en: What we had is most important, loving family.
cues.zh: 我们拥有的最重要的，是一个充满爱的家庭。

cues.en: And I learned from them that hard work is part of life.
cues.zh: 我从他们那里学到，努力工作是生活的一部分。

cues.en: She moved to the States. She developed this really simple idea.
cues.zh: 她搬到了美国，并提出了一个非常简单的想法。

cues.en: Rather than having to make a vaccine idiosyncratic to precisely the virus you're talking about,
cues.zh: 不必为你所说的每一种特定病毒量身定制疫苗，

cues.en: you effectively have this programmable technique to make the protein you want in the body when you want and how you want it.
cues.zh: 你实际上拥有一种可编程技术，能在身体里按你的时间和方式制造你想要的蛋白质。

cues.en: There was loads of work and promise, so you can see why investors wanted to invest in this idea, which is effectively an
cues.zh: 这个方向有大量研究，也充满希望，所以投资者愿意投入这个想法——它本质上是一个

cues.en: idea that you can hack the body to do what you want.
cues.zh: 这种想法是，你可以改造身体，让它按你的意愿行事。

cues.en: It's been decades and decades of research, right?
cues.zh: 这项研究已经持续了几十年，对吧？

cues.en: I mean, essentially, people have been thinking about mRNA ever since sort of when?
cues.zh: 我的意思是，人们大约从什么时候开始思考信使RNA的？

cues.en: Well, she's been going at it since the mid-80s.
cues.zh: 嗯，她从20世纪80年代中期就一直在研究这个。

cues.en: Yeah, it's an obvious thing to go for, and it is one of these very, very alluring ideas.
cues.zh: 是的，这是显而易见的研究方向，也是极具吸引力的想法。

cues.en: But the truth is, it was very hard.
cues.zh: 但事实是，这非常困难。

cues.en: Katalin Karikó was at University of Pennsylvania, and she was, well, as she put it, demoted and forced to retire, effectively.
cues.zh: 卡塔琳·考里科当时在宾夕法尼亚大学；用她自己的话说，她被降职，实际上被迫退休。

cues.en: Before Christmas in 2012, I was told that because I did not get grants, so that I have to pack, and that's how I was terminated there.
cues.zh: 2012年圣诞节前，我被告知因为没拿到资助，必须收拾东西；我就这样被终止聘用。

cues.en: I could also agonize on 24 years hard work, Saturday, Sunday I was there, nobody appreciate, you know, don't do that.
cues.zh: 我也可以为24年的辛苦工作而痛苦，周六周日都在那里，但没人欣赏；你知道，别这样。

cues.en: You have to focus on what next.
cues.zh: 你必须专注于接下来要做什么。

cues.en: So she left for this company called BioNTech. That, you know, it didn't look like a sensible career move.
cues.zh: 于是她去了拜恩泰科公司。你知道，那看起来并不是明智的职业选择。

cues.en: She said, you know, they laughed at me and said BioNTech doesn't even have a website.
cues.zh: 她说，人们嘲笑她，还说拜恩泰科甚至没有网站。

cues.en: In a sense, she left to go to a company that was full of true believers like her.
cues.zh: 从某种意义上说，她去了一个和她一样充满坚定信念者的公司。

cues.en: And come 2019, there were mRNA companies, and all of them were working pretty much on cancer vaccines.
cues.zh: 到了2019年，出现了许多信使RNA公司，它们几乎都在研究癌症疫苗。

cues.en: And there was a lot of money going into this technology, and there were a lot of growing mutterings in the biotech community.
cues.zh: 大量资金投入这项技术，生物科技界也越来越多地议论起来。

cues.en: that it was a hype bubble, that actually this technology still hadn't produced anything or done anything good or useful.
cues.zh: 有人说这是一场炒作泡沫，这项技术至今没有产出任何成果，也没做成任何有益或有用的事。

cues.en: and they'd put billions into it, and maybe it would never happen.
cues.zh: 他们已经投入了数十亿美元，而这一切或许永远不会实现。

cues.en: I think that most people who may have heard this news last week about a possible mRNA cancer vaccine may have recognized this term mRNA and thought, huh?
cues.zh: 我想，上周听说可能有信使RNA癌症疫苗的大多数人，或许都认出了“信使RNA”这个词，并心想：嗯？

cues.en: Does that have something to do with the COVID vaccine? Because that is, I think, the context in which so many of us first heard about mRNA technology.
cues.zh: 这和新冠疫苗有关吗？我想，那正是许多人第一次听说信使RNA技术的背景。

cues.en: And so, Tom, how much did the pandemic accelerate the use of this?
cues.zh: 那么，汤姆，疫情在多大程度上加速了这项技术的应用？

cues.en: We were hugely lucky and didn't realize it.
cues.zh: 我们非常幸运，却没有意识到这一点。

cues.en: As it happened, all of that 30 years of development happened to have just about come to fruition in January of 2020.
cues.zh: 恰恰就在那时，整整30年的研发成果在2020年1月前后终于即将开花结果。

cues.en: I remember chatting to the CEO of BioNTech midway through 2020, and he described how he'd been reading the paper
cues.zh: 我记得2020年年中曾和拜恩泰科的首席执行官聊天，他说自己读到那篇论文时，

cues.en: in early 2020, in January 2020, and decided then, there's something happening.
cues.zh: 那是2020年初、也就是2020年1月；他当时决定：有事情正在发生。

cues.en: This is something we can do something about.
cues.zh: 这是我们能够应对的事情。

cues.en: And he went and had a staff meeting and said, We are no longer a cancer company. We're a COVID company.
cues.zh: 他召集员工开会说：“我们不再是一家癌症公司，而是一家新冠公司。”

cues.en: They switched, you know, a lot of their research to trying to make a rapid COVID vaccine, but that's because they were believers in their technology.
cues.zh: 他们把大量研究转向研发快速的新冠疫苗，因为他们相信自己的技术。

cues.en: A lot of people weren't, because it's never done anything. This has never been a useful technology until it was with COVID.
cues.zh: 很多人并不相信，因为它从未做成过任何事。在新冠疫情之前，这项技术从未真正派上用场。

cues.en: Until it was.
cues.zh: 直到新冠出现。

cues.en: Okay, so you have described a scientific environment in which mRNA seems to be a huge breakthrough success,
cues.zh: 好，你描述了一个科学环境：信使RNA似乎取得了巨大的突破性成功，

cues.en: not just, you know, here in the United States, but around the globe.
cues.zh: 而且不仅是在美国，在全球都是如此。

cues.en: If we look at what happened with the COVID vaccine,
cues.zh: 如果看看新冠疫苗发生了什么，

cues.en: at the same time with COVID, the development of the COVID mRNA vaccines, we also saw the rise of vaccine skepticism.
cues.zh: 我们也会看到，随着新冠和新冠信使RNA疫苗的开发，疫苗怀疑主义兴起了。

cues.en: And one man who really developed a big following during this time period and rose to prominence with his views
cues.zh: 而有一个人在这段时期聚集了大批支持者，也凭借自己的观点声名鹊起，

cues.en: is RFK Jr., who was appointed by President Trump as the Secretary of Health and Human Services.
cues.zh: 那就是小罗伯特·F·肯尼迪，他被特朗普总统任命为美国卫生与公众服务部长。

cues.en: And we have seen him in recent months take direct aim at what he believes is the safety and efficacy of mRNA.
cues.zh: 近几个月，我们看到他直接质疑自己认为的信使RNA安全性和有效性。

cues.en: In August of 2025, he announced that the US government would cancel $500 million worth of funding for mRNA vaccines.
cues.zh: 2025年8月，他宣布美国政府将取消5亿美元的信使RNA疫苗研究经费。

cues.en: He also posted a video online in which he said:
cues.zh: 他还在网上发布视频说：

cues.en: As the pandemic showed us, mRNA vaccines don't perform well against viruses that infect the upper respiratory tract.
cues.zh: 正如疫情所显示的，信使RNA疫苗对感染上呼吸道的病毒效果不佳。

cues.en: And he went on to say that mRNA technology poses more risks than benefits for these respiratory viruses.
cues.zh: 他还说，对于这些呼吸道病毒，信使RNA技术带来的风险超过了收益。

cues.en: Look, I come from a family in which there are many folks who work in science.
cues.zh: 我来自一个有许多人从事科学工作的家庭。

cues.en: I've certainly heard this widely disputed, and RFK is known as a vaccine skeptic.
cues.zh: 我当然听说过，这一说法受到广泛质疑；而且RFK是出了名的疫苗怀疑论者。

cues.en: But can you explain this all to us and the allegations he is making specifically about the efficacy for upper respiratory viruses?
cues.zh: 但你能否向我们解释这一切，以及他针对信使RNA对上呼吸道病毒有效性的指控？

cues.en: Yeah, it's weird, because we're talking about mRNA, which—Which
cues.zh: 是的，这很奇怪，因为我们谈的是信使RNA，而它——它

cues.en: has received a huge boost from the pandemic, scientifically, in terms of prominence, in terms of the ability of these companies to make vaccines.
cues.zh: 在科学上因疫情获得了巨大推动，无论是知名度，还是这些公司制造疫苗的能力。

cues.en: But it's also the case that the yin and the yang of that has also had a huge boost,
cues.zh: 但与之相反的一面也同样得到了巨大推动，

cues.en: and I think probably RFK Jr. wouldn't be here either without the pandemic.
cues.zh: 我想，如果没有疫情，或许也不会有今天的小罗伯特·F·肯尼迪。

cues.en: I remember I was working at The Times during the arrival of those vaccines, and we were looking each day.
cues.zh: 我记得那些疫苗问世时，我正在《泰晤士报》工作，我们每天都在观察。

cues.en: The UK had some of the best data in the world during the pandemic.
cues.zh: 疫情期间，英国拥有世界上最好的数据之一。

cues.en: There's a lot we did wrong, but the data was astonishing.
cues.zh: 我们有很多地方做错了，但数据令人震惊。

cues.en: And you could see the death rate by age
cues.zh: 你可以看到按年龄划分的死亡率

cues.en: group in each day's death data.
cues.zh: 各年龄组每天的死亡数据中。

cues.en: So how many people have been infected and how many people have died?
cues.zh: 那么，有多少人感染，又有多少人死亡？

cues.en: We also knew that we were vaccinating people, starting at the oldest and then working down.
cues.zh: 我们还知道，接种从最年长者开始，再逐步向下推进。

cues.en: And what you saw was this astonishing thing.
cues.zh: 而你看到的是一件惊人的事。

cues.en: In each age group, there would be this sudden dip in the over-85s, this sudden dip in the over-80s, this sudden dip in the over-75s—you could see.
cues.zh: 在每个年龄组中，85岁以上、80岁以上、75岁以上人群的死亡数据都会突然下降，清晰可见。

cues.en: In real time, the effect of the vaccines.
cues.zh: 你能实时看到疫苗的效果。

cues.en: And you were saying you would see a drop in the data once the vaccine was given to that age group.
cues.zh: 你的意思是，一旦给这个年龄组接种疫苗，数据就会下降。

cues.en: Yes, you've got this sort of two-, three-, four-week lag for immunity.
cues.zh: 是的，免疫力大约会延迟两到四周形成。

cues.en: Fatality rate, they've brought it down an order of magnitude.
cues.zh: 死亡率降低了一个数量级。

cues.en: The Health and Human Services Secretary saying that mRNA vaccines don't perform well against viruses that infect the upper respiratory tract,
cues.zh: 卫生与公众服务部长称，mRNA疫苗对感染上呼吸道的病毒效果不佳。

cues.en: and he is saying that the pandemic showed us this.
cues.zh: 他还说，疫情向我们展示了这一点。

cues.en: It sounds like you are saying that is just not accurate.
cues.zh: 听起来，你认为这并不准确。

cues.en: The pandemic actually showed us the efficacy of these vaccines.
cues.zh: 疫情实际上展示了这些疫苗的有效性。

cues.en: I've long since left the situation where I feel like I can change anyone's mind about anything to do with COVID, but it's just not true.
cues.zh: 我早已不再认为自己能改变任何人对新冠的看法，但那种说法就是不正确。

cues.en: The fact is, before the vaccines, in a Western country with the age stratification that you have in the US and the UK,
cues.zh: 事实是，在疫苗出现前，像美国和英国这样按年龄分层的西方国家，

cues.en: you're looking at about 1% overall.
cues.zh: 总体死亡率约为1%。

cues.en: Fatality rate. And afterwards, there wasn't that.
cues.zh: 这是死亡率；而在那之后，就不是这样了。

cues.en: I mean, look, I do think when you have somebody in a high position of authority.
cues.zh: 我是说，当一个人身居高位、拥有很大权威时，

cues.en: In the health department in the United States saying one thing, and you have others in the medical community saying,
cues.zh: 美国卫生部门说一套，而医学界其他人士却说，

cues.en: No, no, this mRNA technology has been effective; it is a scientific breakthrough.
cues.zh: 不，不，这项mRNA技术一直有效，是一项科学突破。

cues.en: People can get confused.
cues.zh: 人们可能会感到困惑。

cues.en: I have another question here about an allegation surrounding these mRNA vaccines,
cues.zh: 我还有一个关于这些mRNA疫苗的指控要问，

cues.en: and that is: are they less safe than other forms of vaccines?
cues.zh: 那就是：它们是否比其他疫苗更不安全？

cues.en: And, Tom, the reason I am asking this is because when the funding for mRNA vaccine research was pulled,
cues.zh: 汤姆，我之所以问这个，是因为mRNA疫苗研究资金被撤回时，

cues.en: the Department of Health and Human Services here in the US issued a statement that said in part that
cues.zh: 美国卫生与公众服务部发表声明，部分内容称，

cues.en: technology that failed to meet current scientific standards would be phased out in favor of evidence-based, ethically grounded solutions
cues.zh: 未达到现行科学标准的技术将被逐步淘汰，转而采用循证且符合伦理的方案，

cues.en: like whole-virus vaccines and novel platforms.
cues.zh: 例如全病毒疫苗和新型平台。

cues.en: So are mRNA vaccines less safe than traditional vaccines?
cues.zh: 那么，mRNA疫苗比传统疫苗更不安全吗？

cues.en: I don't think there is particularly good evidence for that.
cues.zh: 我认为没有特别有力的证据支持这一点。

cues.en: I mean, every intervention has some side effects.
cues.zh: 我是说，每种干预都有一些副作用。

cues.en: If it's going to work, it has side effects.
cues.zh: 如果它能发挥作用，就会有副作用。

cues.en: Every intervention will vary on that.
cues.zh: 不同干预在这方面会有差异。

cues.en: I mean, there is certainly going to be whole-virus vaccines which are far less safe.
cues.zh: 当然，有些全病毒疫苗的安全性会低得多。

cues.en: There were side effects to this. There is myocarditis, pericarditis.
cues.zh: 这类疫苗确实有副作用，包括心肌炎和心包炎。

cues.en: Effects on the heart, they were rare.
cues.zh: 对心脏的影响很少见。

cues.en: They were normally not that severe, but they were present to an extent that,
cues.zh: 这些影响通常并不严重，但确实存在，而且在一定程度上，

cues.en: in the fittest, youngest age groups, at times of low prevalence for COVID, you could make the case that the cost-benefit analysis didn't work.
cues.zh: 在最健康、最年轻的年龄组，且新冠流行率较低时，可以说成本效益分析并不成立。

cues.en: And these were very, very finely balanced arguments.
cues.zh: 这些论点之间的权衡极其微妙。

cues.en: Now, what I would say is, these were signals that were really hard to pick up until you started doing this at population scale.
cues.zh: 我要说的是，直到进行大规模人群研究，这些信号才很难被察觉。

cues.en: And that gives you a sense of how low the side effects were.
cues.zh: 这让你了解副作用有多低。

cues.en: But it would be completely irresponsible to say that they weren't there.
cues.zh: 但说副作用不存在，将是完全不负责任的。

cues.en: But let's park this.
cues.zh: 但我们先把这个问题放一放。

cues.en: So you might think, and I disagree with you, but you might think that the side effects of this weren't worth it
cues.zh: 所以你可能会认为——我不同意——这种副作用不值得，

cues.en: for much of the population for COVID.
cues.zh: 对大多数新冠人群来说不值得。

cues.en: Fine, but what about cancer?
cues.zh: 好吧，但癌症呢？

cues.en: Because even if you think COVID isn't that bad—and for a lot of the population, it isn't that bad,
cues.zh: 因为即使你认为新冠没那么严重——对许多人来说确实如此，

cues.en: it would be my contention that cancer is pretty bad,
cues.zh: 我的观点是，癌症相当严重，

cues.en: and that actually the side effects have to be pretty stonking
cues.zh: 因此副作用必须大到相当惊人，

cues.en: in order for you not to take treatment for cancer,
cues.zh: 你才会不接受癌症治疗，

cues.en: and that is indeed why we do surgery and chemotherapy and radiotherapy and all these things
cues.zh: 这正是我们采用手术、化疗、放疗等各种手段的原因，

cues.en: that you definitely wouldn't do for COVID, but do do them for cancer.
cues.zh: 这些手段对新冠肯定不会用，但会用于癌症。

cues.en: Tom, if we can fast-forward, earlier this month, in August.
cues.zh: 汤姆，我们快进到本月早些时候，也就是八月。

cues.en: The FDA, the Food and Drug Administration, approved the first mRNA flu vaccine made by Moderna,
cues.zh: 美国食品药品监督管理局FDA批准了莫德纳生产的首款mRNA流感疫苗，

cues.en: the same company that is being heralded for this new skin cancer vaccine.
cues.zh: 也就是那家因这款新型皮肤癌疫苗而备受推崇的公司。

cues.en: And my understanding is that initially the FDA had declined to even review Moderna's application
cues.zh: 据我了解，FDA起初甚至拒绝审查莫德纳的申请，

cues.en: for a flu vaccine developed through mRNA technology, but then seemed to reverse course.
cues.zh: 那是通过mRNA技术研发的流感疫苗，但后来FDA似乎改变了方向。

cues.en: Why is that?
cues.zh: 为什么？

cues.en: It's slightly different with the flu vaccine in that we do have a flu vaccine that we use every year
cues.zh: 流感疫苗略有不同，因为我们确实有一种每年使用的流感疫苗，

cues.en: that changes every year with the strain of flu that's circulating.
cues.zh: 它会随当年流行的流感毒株每年变化。

cues.en: Flu changes a lot, so you have to tweak the vaccine each year, and that's done with a traditional vaccine manufacturing technique.
cues.zh: 流感变化很大，所以疫苗必须每年调整，这通过传统的疫苗生产技术完成。

cues.en: So there is less of an impetus to use something fancy and expensive like mRNA, or comparatively expensive.
cues.zh: 因此，使用mRNA这种新颖昂贵、或相对昂贵的技术，动力就没那么大。

cues.en: But the mRNA does offer better strain matching.
cues.zh: 但mRNA确实能更好地匹配毒株。

cues.en: Sometimes you get the strain wrong.
cues.zh: 有时你会选错毒株。

cues.en: What you are generally doing is, you have these flu surveillance people who are looking
cues.zh: 通常的做法是，让流感监测人员观察，

cues.en: at what's happening in Australia during their winter and then trying to fast-forward to what's happening
cues.zh: 澳大利亚冬季的情况，然后推测接下来会发生什么，

cues.en: in the Northern Hemisphere during its winter, and sometimes they get it wrong.
cues.zh: 在北半球冬季的情况；而他们有时会判断错误。

cues.en: Whereas with mRNA, you can match better and you can move more nimbly.
cues.zh: 而使用mRNA，匹配会更准确，调整也更灵活。

cues.en: So I think there was—there was elements of politics.
cues.zh: 所以我认为，这其中确实有政治因素。

cues.en: The word mRNA has become...
cues.zh: “mRNA”这个词已经变得……

cues.en: political in a way that isn't helpful.
cues.zh: 这种政治化并没有帮助。

cues.en: And I don't want to speak to the FDA's particular decisions on the flu vaccine because I am not across it,
cues.zh: 我不想评论 FDA 在流感疫苗上的具体决定，因为我并不了解相关情况。

cues.en: but I would say that there are advantages of the mRNA, but there is less of a compelling public health case than there might be in other uses of it.
cues.zh: 但我想说，信使 RNA 确有优势；只是与它的其他用途相比，用于流感疫苗的公共卫生理由没那么有说服力。

cues.en: From where I sit in the United States, Tom, it seems like there are two conversations happening at one time around mRNA technology.
cues.zh: 汤姆，以我在美国的观察，围绕信使 RNA 技术似乎同时存在两种讨论。

cues.en: There is the scientific conversation, and in a previous life, in fact, I used to cover some biotech.
cues.zh: 一种是科学层面的讨论。事实上，我以前曾报道过一些生物科技。

cues.en: I was based in Cambridge, Massachusetts, and, you know, I remember interviewing one of the co-founders of Moderna.
cues.zh: 当时我常驻马萨诸塞州剑桥，也记得曾采访过莫德纳的一位联合创始人。

cues.en: This was years ago,
cues.zh: 那已经是多年前的事了。

cues.en: and there were many people in and around that ecosystem really excited about the potential of this type of technology.
cues.zh: 当时那个生态圈内外有许多人都对这类技术的潜力感到非常兴奋。

cues.en: And that continues to exist, right?
cues.zh: 这种热情现在依然存在，对吧？

cues.en: And then on the other side, as we've discussed, there's this political conversation we're having with RFK Jr.
cues.zh: 而另一方面，正如我们所讨论的，我们还在围绕小罗伯特·F·肯尼迪展开政治层面的讨论。

cues.en: And his decision to cancel half a billion dollars' worth of funding for mRNA research.
cues.zh: 以及他决定取消总额五亿美元的信使 RNA 研究经费。

cues.en: You know, earlier we mentioned Dr Karikó, who helped develop this technology.
cues.zh: 我们之前提到过帮助开发这项技术的卡塔琳·考里科博士。

cues.en: She went on to later win the Nobel Prize along with her research partner.
cues.zh: 后来，她与自己的研究伙伴共同获得了诺贝尔奖。

cues.en: And when these funding cuts were announced last year, she spoke with my colleagues here at the BBC, in which she said:
cues.zh: 去年这些削减经费的措施宣布后，她接受了我在 BBC 同事的采访。她说：

cues.en: It's a huge, huge mistake. It was based on misinformation.
cues.zh: 这是一个巨大的、巨大的错误，依据的是错误信息。

cues.en: And not evidence. He ignored evidence, he ignored facts,
cues.zh: 而不是证据。他无视证据，也无视事实。

cues.en: and the US ability to develop vaccine during the next pandemic suffers tremendously.
cues.zh: 这会严重削弱美国在下一次大流行期间研发疫苗的能力。

cues.en: In her view:
cues.zh: 在她看来：

cues.en: I was moving to the United States from Hungary.
cues.zh: 我当时正从匈牙利搬到美国。

cues.en: When I couldn't do my work here in the US, I moved to another country.
cues.zh: 当我无法在美国继续工作时，我就搬去了另一个国家。

cues.en: So it seems that scientists need to move to another country
cues.zh: 所以看来，科学家需要搬到另一个国家，

cues.en: if they want to advance in this messenger RNA vaccine field.
cues.zh: 如果他们想在信使 RNA 疫苗领域取得进展。

cues.en: So this is a national-security issue; the US will suffer.
cues.zh: 所以这是一个国家安全问题，美国将因此受损。

cues.en: So what does it mean for Americans if the government chooses not to fund these technologies?
cues.zh: 那么，如果政府选择不给这些技术提供资金，这对美国人意味着什么？

cues.en: Look, she's devoted her career to this, so perhaps unsurprisingly she was cross and baffled.
cues.zh: 她毕生致力于这项事业，所以她感到恼火和困惑，也许并不奇怪。

cues.en: And she moved from Hungary in order to do her science.
cues.zh: 她当初离开匈牙利，就是为了从事自己的科学研究。

cues.en: So there are plenty of other people who are far less constrained who will pick up sticks and move to do the science where it works.
cues.zh: 所以，还有许多约束少得多的人，他们会收拾行囊，搬到能够开展这项研究的地方。

cues.en: But if there's another pandemic and it's a worse virus,
cues.zh: 但如果再次发生大流行，而且病毒更加危险，

cues.en: and actually we can make a vaccine quite easily using mRNA,
cues.zh: 而我们其实可以利用信使 RNA 很容易地制造疫苗，

cues.en: people are going to have to rather rapidly re-evaluate their views.
cues.zh: 人们将不得不相当迅速地重新评估自己的看法。

cues.en: And I suspect having a US that has pulled out of research,
cues.zh: 我想，一个退出研究的美国，

cues.en: probably pulled out of the sort of manufacturing that would be required to make those vaccines at scale,
cues.zh: 很可能也会退出大规模生产这类疫苗所需的制造环节，

cues.en: will be bad for the US and ultimately very bad for the world as well.
cues.zh: 这对美国不利，最终也会对全世界非常不利。

cues.en: But you've got plenty of private companies,
cues.zh: 但美国有许多私营企业，

cues.en: and you've got, particularly in Cambridge, the world's leading biotech scene with a bunch of investors.
cues.zh: 尤其是在剑桥，还有全球领先的生物科技产业，以及一批投资者。

cues.en: So I suspect you will find that there is plenty of money swirling around.
cues.zh: 所以我想，你会发现市场上有大量资金在流动。

cues.en: I think a very easy argument for someone like RFK Jr.
cues.zh: 我认为，对小罗伯特·F·肯尼迪这样的人来说，一个很容易提出的说法是：

cues.en: to make is actually, look:
cues.zh: 其实就是：你看，

cues.en: I don't think this works terribly well in viruses.
cues.zh: 我不认为这项技术用于病毒时效果很好。

cues.en: I don't think it's worth the risk in viruses.
cues.zh: 我不认为在病毒领域值得冒这个风险。

cues.en: And I will reflect—you know, I'm making this case, I disagree, and I want to say I disagree, but it's an easy argument to make.
cues.zh: 我也要说明，虽然我是在提出这个说法，但我并不同意，而且我想明确说我不同意；只是这个说法很容易提出。

cues.en: Say, a virus that doesn't kill many people, comparatively, I don't think we should be giving them this new technology.
cues.zh: 比如说，某种病毒相对而言不会造成很多人死亡，我不认为我们应该把这项新技术用于它们。

cues.en: It is a far easier argument to make, but cancer is a different issue.
cues.zh: 这种说法容易得多，但癌症是另一回事。

cues.en: Obviously, the risk-benefit changes completely.
cues.zh: 显然，风险与收益的权衡完全不同。

cues.en: So I suspect you might well see that pivot.
cues.zh: 所以我想，你很可能会看到这种转向。

cues.en: Because I suspect that the US will want to keep on funding this stuff.
cues.zh: 因为我想，美国会希望继续为这些研究提供资金。

cues.en: Well, Tom, thank you for taking the time to walk us through this all and help us try to make sense of it.
cues.zh: 汤姆，谢谢你抽出时间为我们梳理这一切，帮助我们理解这个问题。

cues.en: Appreciate it. Cheers.
cues.zh: 谢谢你。谢了。

cues.en: That was Tom Whipple, host of the BBC's Inside Science program and a writer for the Times of London.
cues.zh: 刚才是汤姆·惠普尔，他是 BBC《Inside Science》节目的主持人，也是《泰晤士报》伦敦版的作者。

cues.en: We contacted the Department of Health and Human Services for comment.
cues.zh: 我们联系了美国卫生与公众服务部，请其置评。

cues.en: They responded in part, quote:
cues.zh: 对方部分回应如下：

cues.en: Secretary Kennedy has been clear that he believes that mRNA products warrant heightened scientific scrutiny.
cues.zh: 肯尼迪部长明确表示，他认为信使 RNA 产品需要接受更严格的科学审查。

cues.en: HHS continues to support mRNA research where the science shows promise, including for hard-to-treat cancers.
cues.zh: 美国卫生与公众服务部将继续支持有科学前景的信使 RNA 研究，包括针对难以治疗的癌症的研究。

cues.zh: 和往常一样，如果你有问题、投诉或选题建议，随时可以通过《全球故事》联系​​我们。

cues.zh: 本期节目由露西·保罗和萨姆·钱塔拉-萨克制作。

cues.zh: 混音：特拉维斯·埃文斯。

cues.zh: 数字制片人是萨姆·格鲁埃。

cues.zh: 执行制片人是詹姆斯·希尔德，资深新闻编辑是柴娜·柯林斯。

cues.zh: 我是阿斯玛·哈立德。

cues.zh: 一如既往，感谢你抽时间陪伴我们。我们明天再见。
